title: Record Few Americans Say College Is Very Important
paragraphs: For many years, going to college was seen as one of the most important steps to success in the United States. But according to a new Gallup poll, fewer Americans than ever believe that a college education is very important.

The poll was carried out in August 2026 through telephone interviews with 1,200 adults, and the results were published in October. It found that only 31% of Americans now say a college education is "very important." That is the lowest number since Gallup first asked the question in 1978. It is also lower than last year's figure of 35%, which was the previous record low.

The change over the past decade has been dramatic. In 2013, 70% of Americans said college was very important. Meanwhile, the share of people who say college is "not too important" has risen from just 6% in 2013 to 29% today. The largest group, 39%, now says college is "fairly important."

According to Gallup, the decline has happened in every group it tracks, including different ages, political parties and education levels. However, some groups changed more than others. For example, only 22% of Republicans now say college is very important, down from 41% in 2019.

So what is behind this big change? Megan Brenan, a senior editor at Gallup, said the results may be partly explained by Americans' increasing concerns about the cost of college. A separate poll by Gallup and the Lumina Foundation found that about two-thirds of people think colleges are doing a poor job of providing an affordable education.

However, many Americans still see some real value in a degree. In the Lumina Foundation and Gallup study, 73% of workers without a college degree, and 69% of college graduates, said earning a degree is at least as important as it was 20 years ago.
